title: Slow Cooker Feijoada

overview.description: A rich Brazilian black bean and pork stew slowly cooked with pork shoulder, smoked sausage, bacon and aromatic vegetables.

ingredients: 500g pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
method: Soak the beans in plenty of cold water overnight.
Drain and rinse the beans before cooking.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan.
Fry the bacon until it has released some of its fat.
Add the pork shoulder and pork belly in batches and brown lightly.
Transfer the pork and bacon to the slow cooker.
Add the onions and cook until softened.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Transfer the onions and garlic to the slow cooker.
Add the soaked beans, bay leaves, chorizo and orange quarters.
Pour in enough stock to cover the ingredients.
Cook on LOW for 8–10 hours, or until the beans and pork are completely tender.
Remove the orange quarters and bay leaves.
If the stew is thinner than desired, remove the lid and cook on HIGH for a short period, or mash some of the beans into the sauce.

learning.did-you-know: Feijoada is one of Brazil's best-known dishes and is traditionally associated with black beans cooked slowly with pork and other meats. It is commonly served with rice, greens, orange and farofa.
learning.what-you-will-learn: How dried beans absorb water and soften during slow cooking, and how long, gentle cooking allows tough cuts of meat to become tender.

notes.why-its-in-the-chapman-kitchen: A substantial one-pot meal that is ideal for slow cooking and batch preparation, while introducing a classic Brazilian dish to the meal rotation.
chapman-tips: Use a large slow cooker because the recipe makes a generous batch.
Soaking the beans overnight reduces the cooking time and helps them cook more evenly.
Browning the pork and bacon first adds extra depth of flavour.
The orange is used to add fragrance and balance rather than to make the stew taste strongly of orange.
Don't add acidic ingredients until the beans are tender, as acidity can slow the softening of beans.
If using very salty smoked sausage or bacon, season cautiously until the end.
The stew often tastes even better after resting overnight.
For a thicker sauce, mash some of the beans against the side of the pot and stir them through.
notes.batch-cooking: Freezes very well. Cool thoroughly, portion and freeze in airtight containers.
notes.leftovers: Keeps well in the refrigerator and often tastes even better the following day.
